title: Information Disclosure - Unauthenticated Scan Status Access
description: The GET /status/{scan_id} SSE endpoint verifies that the scan_id exists in event_buses but does NOT verify that the requesting user owns or has access to the scan. Any authenticated user can monitor the real-time progress of any other user's scans by knowing the scan_id, exposing sensitive audit details, findings, and agent logs.
suggested_fix: Add authorization check: verify that request.state.user_id owns the scan by querying the database for the scan_report and validating ownership before streaming any events.

title: Broken Access Control - IDOR in FORGE Fix Endpoint
description: The POST /api/fix endpoint validates that the action_item belongs to the authenticated user but does NOT validate that the associated scan_report and project also belong to the user. An attacker could potentially trigger FORGE remediation on other users' action items by manipulating the action_item_id.

locations.snippet:
action_item = await db.get_action_item(request_body.action_item_id, user_id)
if not action_item:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, ...)
...
project_id = UUID(action_item["project_id"])
project = await db.get_project(project_id)
...
scan_report_id = UUID(action_item["scan_report_id"])
scan_report = await db.get_scan_report(scan_report_id, user_id)

suggested_fix: After fetching scan_report, add explicit authorization check: validate that scan_report['user_id'] matches request.state.user_id before proceeding. Also validate project ownership.

title: Sandbox Command Injection Risk via Repo URL
description: The primer endpoint passes user-supplied repo_url to SandboxManager.provision() and executes arbitrary shell commands (find, ls, git) on the cloned repository. While the sandbox aims to isolate execution, a malicious repository could contain malicious scripts that execute during the cloning or file listing process. Additionally, there's no validation that the repository URL is from an allowed domain/owner.

locations.snippet:
await sandbox_mgr.provision(scan_id, repo_info.clone_url)
tree = await sandbox_mgr.exec(scan_id, "find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' ...")
top_dirs = await sandbox_mgr.exec(scan_id, "ls -1", timeout=15)
head = await sandbox_mgr.exec(scan_id, "git rev-parse HEAD", timeout=15)

suggested_fix: Implement repository allowlist/blocklist validation. Use a dedicated sandbox with minimal privileges and no network access beyond cloning. Add timeout limits and resource quotas. Consider pre-cloning trusted repositories only.

title: Webhook Replay Protection Can Be Disabled
description: The _register_delivery function uses settings.webhook_replay_window_seconds to determine replay protection window. If this setting is set to 0 or a very small value, the replay protection mechanism becomes ineffective, allowing rapid duplicate webhook submissions.

locations.snippet:
async def _register_delivery(delivery_id: str) -> bool:
    """Return False when a duplicate delivery ID is observed inside replay window."""
    now_ts = int(time.time())
    ttl_seconds = max(60, int(settings.webhook_replay_window_seconds))

suggested_fix: Enforce a minimum replay window of 60 seconds in code (already done via max(60,...)). Add validation at startup to ensure the setting cannot be disabled or set below minimum.

title: OAuth State Secret Falls Back to JWT Secret
description: The _state_secret() function returns github_oauth_state_secret if configured, otherwise falls back to supabase_jwt_secret. This weakens OAuth state security since the JWT secret is used for many purposes and may be rotated more frequently. Additionally, if neither is set, the system may fail unsafely.
suggested_fix: Require github_oauth_state_secret to be explicitly configured and non-empty. Add validation at application startup if OAuth is enabled.

title: Rate Limiting Bypass via IP Spoofing
description: The rate limiter uses get_remote_address() from slowapi which extracts IP from request.client.host. This can be easily bypassed by attackers spoofing X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP headers, as the code doesn't validate or use these headers securely.

locations.snippet:
from slowapi import Limiter
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)

def rate_limit_string() -> str:
    """Return the rate limit string for the configured limit."""
    return f"{settings.rate_limit_per_minute}/minute"

suggested_fix: Implement a custom key_func that properly handles X-Forwarded-For only when behind a trusted reverse proxy, or use a more robust identifier like session-based rate limiting combined with IP.

title: Missing Input Validation on Pydantic Request Models
description: Cross-segment analysis identified missing input validation: AgentLogEntry.message has no length limits (DoS), Finding.code_snippet has no sanitization (XSS), ProjectIntake fields lack validation. While these models are defined in other segments, this API segment uses them without additional validation.

locations.snippet:

    request: Request,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,

suggested_fix: Add explicit validation at route handlers for critical fields: max length on message/code_snippet, sanitize code content before storage, validate nested objects in project_intake.

title: JWT Algorithm Not Restricted to HS256
description: The JWT verification in auth.py explicitly specifies algorithms=["HS256"] which is correct. However, if settings.supabase_jwt_secret is ever changed to None or empty, the jwt.decode call would fail unexpectedly. Additionally, there's no validation that the JWT secret meets minimum entropy requirements.

locations.snippet:
payload = jwt.decode(
    token,
    settings.supabase_jwt_secret,
    algorithms=["HS256"],
    audience="authenticated",
)

suggested_fix: Add validation at startup to ensure supabase_jwt_secret is set and meets minimum length/entropy requirements. Consider supporting RS256 for future Supabase Auth changes.

title: No Rate Limiting on Onboarding Endpoint
description: The POST /api/onboarding/org endpoint has no rate limiting decorator, unlike other sensitive endpoints like /audit, /fix, and /github-oauth. This could allow unlimited org onboarding submissions.
suggested_fix: Add @limiter.limit(rate_limit_string()) decorator to the save_org_onboarding endpoint for consistency with other endpoints.

title: Missing Onboarding Check in Primer Endpoint
description: The POST /api/primer endpoint does not check if onboarding is complete before proceeding. This bypasses the onboarding requirement enforced in _tier1_preflight for the audit endpoint. A user who hasn't completed onboarding could still have primer data generated.

locations.snippet:
@router.post("/primer", response_model=PrimerResponse)
async def run_primer(request_body: PrimerRequest, request: Request) -> PrimerResponse:
    user_id: str = request.state.user_id

    github_token = await db.get_github_access_token(user_id)

suggested_fix: Add onboarding check at the beginning of run_primer: if not await db.is_onboarding_complete(user_id): raise HTTPException(403, detail='Onboarding required')

title: Memory leak in event_buses SSE storage
description: The global event_buses dict in api/routes/_sse.py accumulates entries for completed scans indefinitely. There's no cleanup mechanism, leading to unbounded memory growth over time. Each scan adds a list that is never removed after the SSE stream completes.
suggested_fix: Add cleanup logic to remove scan entries from event_buses after SSE stream completes. Consider using弱引用 or a dedicated cleanup background task that purges old entries older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 1 hour).

title: Unbounded memory growth in webhook replay detection
description: The _seen_deliveries dict in api/routes/webhook.py grows indefinitely. Although there's cleanup logic for expired entries, if settings.webhook_replay_window_seconds is very large, the dict could consume significant memory. Additionally, the cleanup runs inside _register_delivery which may not be called frequently enough.
suggested_fix: Move the cleanup to a periodic background task instead of doing it on every delivery. Consider using an LRU cache with TTL or a time-bucketed structure to limit memory usage more predictably.

title: Global mutable counter for cleanup scheduling
description: The _scan_start_counter global variable in api/routes/audit.py is used to trigger periodic cleanup. This pattern is problematic for testing (non-deterministic behavior), doesn't work in multi-process deployments, and has race conditions in async contexts.
suggested_fix: Replace global counter with a time-based approach: run cleanup if the last cleanup was more than N minutes ago. Use a timestamp stored in the database or a time-based check to trigger cleanup deterministically.

title: Missing input validation on repo_url across endpoints
description: Multiple endpoints accept repo_url as string without validation: api/routes/audit.py, api/routes/primer.py. Only primer.py uses Pydantic HttpUrl which provides validation, but audit.py passes through raw strings. This could allow malformed URLs to propagate to downstream services.
suggested_fix: Add repo_url validation using Pydantic's HttpUrl type in AuditRequest and FixRequest models. Ensure consistent validation across all endpoints that accept repository URLs.

title: Large hardcoded prompt with potential token overflow
description: In api/routes/primer.py, the _summarize function constructs a prompt with up to 15000 characters of JSON: 'json.dumps(primer_json)[:15000]'. Many LLM APIs have lower max token limits, and this could cause API failures or be truncated unexpectedly.

locations.snippet:
prompt = (

        "1) likely product purpose\n"
        "2) likely core user flows\n"
        "3) likely deployment/runtime shape\n"
        "4) top immediate audit risk areas\n"
        "Keep it concise and factual.\n\n"
        f"{json.dumps(primer_json)[:15000]}"
    )

suggested_fix: Add a more conservative truncation limit (e.g., 4000 chars) and consider implementing proper token counting if available. Alternatively, extract key fields from primer_json rather than dumping the entire JSON.

title: Magic numbers scattered throughout primer.py
description: Multiple hardcoded magic numbers in api/routes/primer.py without explanation: 350 (file count), 30/15 (timeouts), 12 (scripts limit), 20 (dependencies limit), 200/40 (sample limits), 280 (max tokens). These should be constants or configuration values.
suggested_fix: Create a configuration class or constants module with documented values for all these limits. Example: MAX_FILE_TREE_SIZE = 350, MAX_DEPS_SAMPLE = 20, etc.

title: Complex function with multiple responsibilities
description: The start_audit function in api/routes/audit.py (lines 164-214) performs too many distinct tasks: authentication check, scan ID generation, event bus initialization, GitHub token retrieval, preflight validation, project creation, and scan creation. This violates the Single Responsibility Principle and makes testing difficult.

locations.snippet:

    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,

suggested_fix: Refactor into smaller functions: _initialize_audit_context(), _validate_and_prepare_project(), _create_scan_record(). This improves testability and makes error handling more granular.

title: Missing error handling for external service dependencies
description: In api/routes/audit.py, if db.get_github_access_token() fails or returns None, the code proceeds to use github_token which could be None, leading to downstream failures with less clear error messages. Similarly, db operations in preflight don't have consistent error handling.

suggested_fix: Add explicit checks after db.get_github_access_token() and raise clear HTTPException if GitHub connection is required but missing. Consider requiring GitHub connection as part of onboarding rather than handling it lazily.

title: Inconsistent exception handling patterns
description: The codebase has inconsistent exception handling: some routes catch HTTPException and re-raise (line 200-201 in audit.py), others use broad except clauses. The github_oauth.py has verbose manual status code checks instead of using resp.raise_for_status().
suggested_fix: Standardize exception handling: use resp.raise_for_status() for httpx responses. Remove redundant HTTPException re-raise pattern - let them propagate naturally. Add a global exception handler for consistent error responses.

title: No SSE connection limit or rate limiting
description: The /api/status/{scan_id} endpoint in api/routes/status.py allows unlimited SSE connections without rate limiting or per-user connection limits. This could be exploited for resource exhaustion.

locations.snippet:
@router.get("/status/{scan_id}")
async def stream_status(scan_id: UUID, request: Request):

suggested_fix: Add @limiter.limit decorator to the status endpoint similar to other routes. Consider adding per-user concurrent connection limits using a connection counter.

title: Dynamic import inside background task function
description: In api/routes/fix.py, the trigger_forge_remediate import is done inside the _run_forge_fix function rather than at module level. This delays the error and makes it harder to test the import at module load time.
suggested_fix: Move the import to module level at the top of the file. If the import needs to be conditional due to optional FORGE functionality, handle the ImportError at module load with a clear message.

title: Missing null safety on dictionary access
description: Multiple places access dictionary keys without null checks. In audit.py line 131: existing_project['id'] is accessed after the None check, but preflight['existing_project'] is used directly without guaranteed existence. Similar issues with tier1_findings in fix.py.

locations.snippet:
project_id = (

            if preflight["existing_project"]
            else await db.get_or_create_project(

suggested_fix: Use .get() with default values consistently. Consider using Pydantic models for scan_report to get type-safe access with validation.

title: Global in-memory state for SSE event buses lacks cleanup and doesn't scale horizontally
description: The event_buses dictionary in api/routes/_sse.py stores scan events in global in-memory state. This creates memory leaks as scans are never explicitly removed from the dict. Additionally, this approach doesn't work in horizontally scaled deployments where multiple API instances maintain separate in-memory stores, causing clients connected to different instances to miss events. There's no TTL mechanism for old scan data.
suggested_fix: Replace in-memory event_buses with Redis or another distributed cache. Implement periodic cleanup of stale scan entries or use TTL-based expiration. This ensures horizontal scaling and prevents memory leaks.

title: Layering violation: Routes directly import and instantiate domain objects from other segments
description: Routes in api/routes/audit.py directly import domain objects from seg-tier1-6 (DeterministicIndexer, Tier1Orchestrator, Tier1Quota) and instantiate them within route handlers. This violates clean architecture principles where the presentation layer (routes) should not contain business logic. The tier1 orchestrator contains substantial business logic that should be accessed through a service abstraction layer. This creates tight coupling and makes the API layer dependent on internal domain structures.

locations.snippet:
from tier1.indexer import DeterministicIndexer
from tier1.orchestrator import Tier1Orchestrator
from tier1.quota import get_quota_status, utc_month_key

orchestrator = Tier1Orchestrator(
            scan_id=scan_id,
            repo_url=str(request.repo_url),
            project_id=project_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            project_intake=request.project_intake.model_dump(mode="json"),
            primer=request.primer,
            emit=emit,
            github_token=github_token,
            user_preferences=user_preferences,
            run_context={...},
        )

suggested_fix: Create a service abstraction layer (e.g., AuditService) that encapsulates tier1 orchestration. Routes should call service methods rather than directly instantiating domain objects. This improves testability and maintains proper layer boundaries.

title: Direct database access in route handlers violates persistence layer abstraction
description: All route handlers in this segment directly import and call methods from services.supabase_client (aliased as db). This creates tight coupling between the API layer and the persistence layer. If the database technology changes, all route files would need modification. There's no repository pattern or service layer abstraction protecting the routes from database implementation details.

locations.snippet: from services import supabase_client as db
from services import supabase_client as db
from services import supabase_client as db

suggested_fix: Introduce a repository interface or service layer that abstracts database operations. Create interfaces like IAuditRepository, IProjectRepository that the routes depend on, with SupabaseClient implementing these interfaces.

title: Direct coupling to sandbox manager in route layer
description: api/routes/primer.py directly imports and instantiates SandboxManager, managing its lifecycle (provision, exec, destroy) within the route handler. This couples the API layer directly to infrastructure concerns. The sandbox management should be abstracted through a service that handles provisioning, execution, and cleanup lifecycle.
suggested_fix: Create a SandboxService that manages sandbox lifecycle. Routes should call service methods like run_primer(scan_id, repo_url) rather than managing sandbox instances directly. This improves error handling, ensures proper cleanup on failures, and enables easier testing.

title: Global state for webhook delivery replay detection
description: The webhook route uses module-level dictionaries (_seen_deliveries) for replay attack detection. This global state has the same issues as event_buses: it doesn't work across multiple API instances and will have inconsistent replay detection in horizontally scaled deployments.
suggested_fix: Replace the in-memory dict with Redis for distributed replay detection. This ensures consistent replay protection across all API instances.

title: Cross-segment circular dependency risk through shared state
description: This segment imports from tier1 module (Tier1Orchestrator, DeterministicIndexer) while the tier1 segment likely imports models from seg-models-1. If the audit route handlers were to be imported by models or if error handling logic were added that triggers model validation during orchestration, this could create circular dependencies. The tight cross-segment coupling increases this risk.

locations.snippet:
from tier1.indexer import DeterministicIndexer
from tier1.orchestrator import Tier1Orchestrator

suggested_fix: Introduce service boundaries that clearly separate segment responsibilities. Use dependency injection to avoid direct imports between segments. Consider using protocol/interface definitions to decouple implementations.

title: Inconsistent cleanup strategy for background tasks
description: The tier1 expired data cleanup uses a counter-based approach (_scan_start_counter) that triggers every N scans. This is non-deterministic and may lead to inconsistent cleanup timing. Additionally, there's no error handling for failed cleanup operations - exceptions are logged but not surfaced for monitoring. The finding mentions duplicate utc_now functions in neighboring segments, which suggests inconsistent time handling patterns could affect this cleanup logic.

locations.snippet:
async def _maybe_cleanup_tier1() -> None:
    global _scan_start_counter
    _scan_start_counter += 1
    if _scan_start_counter % _CLEANUP_EVERY_N_SCANS == 0:
        await cleanup_tier1_expired()

suggested_fix: Replace counter-based cleanup with time-based scheduling (e.g., APScheduler or background task running at intervals). Add monitoring metrics for cleanup failures. Address the utc_now inconsistency by centralizing time utilities.

title: Missing input sanitization on LLM prompt construction
description: The primer route builds prompts for the LLM by directly interpolating repository data (file_tree_sample, dependency_sample, npm_scripts) into the prompt string. While this is in the API layer, unsanitized input could lead to prompt injection if a malicious repository name or dependency is provided. This relates to security findings in neighboring segments about missing input validation.

locations.snippet:
prompt = (
        "You are Agent_Primer. Summarize this repository context in 4 short bullets:\n"
        "1) likely product purpose\n"
        "2) likely core user flows\n"
        "3) likely deployment/runtime shape\n"
        "4) top immediate audit risk areas\n"
        "Keep it concise and factual.\n\n"
        f"{json.dumps(primer_json)[:15000]}"
    )

suggested_fix: Implement input sanitization before including repository data in prompts. Consider using a structured format (JSON) rather than raw string concatenation. Add validation on repository data extraction to limit size and prevent injection.

title: Token decoding using settings directly in middleware without abstraction
description: The SupabaseAuthMiddleware directly uses settings.supabase_jwt_secret for token decoding. The middleware is tightly coupled to configuration values. If token validation logic needs to change (e.g., different algorithms, audience validation), the middleware must be modified. This is a minor violation of separation of concerns.

                settings.supabase_jwt_secret,
                algorithms=["HS256"],
                audience="authenticated",

suggested_fix: Extract token validation into an AuthService that can be injected. The middleware should call the service rather than directly accessing settings. This improves testability and allows for easier modification of auth logic.

title: Hardcoded magic values and enum-like string literals throughout routes
description: Multiple places in the routes use hardcoded strings that should be enums or constants: status codes in HTTPException, scan tiers ('free'), event types, and status values. This is related to the quality finding about inconsistent status representation and missing enum constraints in neighboring segments. The routes should use centralized constants or enums for better maintainability.
suggested_fix: Create centralized enums/constants for status codes, scan tiers, and fix attempt statuses. Import and use these consistently across all route handlers. This aligns with the quality improvement recommendations for neighboring segments.

title: Missing Input Validation on Secret Value Field
description: The SecretCreateRequest model in models/program.py has a 'value' field with no validation constraints. This allows arbitrarily large strings to be passed as secret values, which could cause denial-of-service issues when processing or storing these secrets. Additionally, without validation, the secret value could contain malformed data that might cause issues in downstream cryptographic operations.
suggested_fix: Add validation constraints to the value field: value: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=10000). Consider also validating character encoding and format based on the expected secret type.

title: Unrestricted Severity Field Allows Arbitrary Values
description: The DebtItemRequest model has a 'severity' field that defaults to 'medium' but accepts any string value without validation. This could lead to inconsistent data and potential issues in downstream processing that expects specific severity values. An attacker or misconfigured client could inject arbitrary severity values that bypass business logic checks.

locations.snippet:
class DebtItemRequest(BaseModel):
    node_id: str
    summary: str
    severity: str = "medium"

suggested_fix: Convert severity to an Enum or use a Literal type with allowed values: severity: Literal['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low'] = 'medium'

title: Unrestricted Policy Violation Code Field
description: The PolicyViolationRequest model accepts an unrestricted 'code' string without validation. This could allow injection of malformed or malicious policy codes that bypass security checks in downstream policy enforcement logic.

locations.snippet:
class PolicyViolationRequest(BaseModel):
    code: str
    message: str
    source: str = "policy_engine"
    blocking: bool = True

suggested_fix: Add validation constraints to the code field: code: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100, pattern=r'^[A-Z0-9_]+$')

title: Unrestricted Secret Name Field Could Enable Path Traversal
description: The SecretCreateRequest model accepts a 'name' field without validation. If this name is used in file system operations or as part of lookup keys in external systems, it could potentially be exploited for path traversal or injection attacks. The field should have validation to restrict allowed characters.
suggested_fix: Add validation to restrict the name field: name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200, pattern=r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$')

title: Duplicate utc_now function across multiple model files
description: The utc_now() function is duplicated verbatim in models/builds.py (line 16), models/program.py (line 14), and models/runtime.py (line 13). This violates the DRY principle and creates maintenance burden. If timezone handling needs to be updated, all three locations must be modified.
suggested_fix: Create a shared utils module (e.g., models/_utils.py) with the utc_now function and import it from all three files. Alternatively, use Pydantic's built-in timezone support with field(default_factory=datetime.now, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

title: Inconsistent timestamp default_factory patterns
description: Different model files use different approaches for default timestamps: models/agent_log.py uses lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc), while models/builds.py, program.py, and runtime.py use a custom utc_now() function. This inconsistency makes the codebase harder to maintain and understand.
suggested_fix: Standardize on a single approach - either use a shared utc_now function or leverage Pydantic's date utilities. The shared utility approach is recommended for consistency across the codebase.

title: Missing input validation on string fields
description: Several Pydantic models have string fields without length constraints, which could lead to unbounded data storage. Specifically: Finding.title and Finding.description have no max_length; ActionItem.title, ActionItem.description, and ActionItem.effort lack validation. Also, DebtItem.severity and PolicyViolation.message are plain strings without enum constraints.

locations.snippet:

    description: str
    effort: str = "moderate"

suggested_fix: Add Field constraints: title=Field(max_length=200), description=Field(max_length=5000), effort should be an Enum (quick|moderate|significant), severity should use Severity enum or Field(max_length=50)

title: Missing URL validation on repo_url field
description: BuildRun model has a repo_url field as plain str with no validation. This should be an HttpUrl to ensure valid URL format and prevent injection attacks or malformed data.
suggested_fix: Change to repo_url: HttpUrl from pydantic import HttpUrl, similar to AuditRequest.repo_url which correctly uses HttpUrl

title: Inconsistent Enum naming conventions
description: The codebase uses inconsistent Enum value naming: BuildStatus uses lowercase ('pending', 'completed'), GateType uses SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE ('MERGE_GATE', 'TEST_GATE'), and TaskStatus uses lowercase. This inconsistency makes the API unpredictable and harder to use. Also, LogLevel includes 'success' which is not a standard log level.

suggested_fix: Standardize all Enum values to one convention (preferably lowercase for consistency with HTTP status conventions). Remove 'success' from LogLevel or document why it's needed. Consider using consistent naming across all enums.

title: Missing Validation on Effort Field in ActionItem
description: ActionItem.effort is a string field with a default value of 'moderate' but no validation to ensure only valid values ('quick', 'moderate', 'significant') are accepted. This could lead to inconsistent data.
suggested_fix: Create an EffortLevel Enum: class EffortLevel(str, Enum): quick = "quick", moderate = "moderate", significant = "significant", then use effort: EffortLevel = EffortLevel.moderate

title: Plain string severity in DebtItem lacks validation
description: DebtItem model uses a plain string for severity with default 'medium' but no constraints on valid values. PolicyViolation also has a plain string for message without length validation.
suggested_fix: Use the Severity enum from models/findings.py for DebtItem.severity. Add max_length to PolicyViolation.message: message: str = Field(max_length=2000)

title: Large model with many optional fields lacks validation
description: BuildRun is a large model with 14 fields including nested lists. Several fields like metadata, dag, task_runs have no validation on their contents. The metadata field accepts any dict which could lead to storing arbitrary unstructured data.

suggested_fix: Consider adding validation schemas for metadata, or creating separate TypedDict definitions. Consider breaking BuildRun into smaller composition models if it grows further.

title: Missing field validation in RuntimeSession metadata
description: RuntimeSession.metadata uses plain dict with no type constraints. This is inconsistent with RuntimeMetric which properly uses dict[str, str] for tags.
suggested_fix: Use dict[str, Any] for flexibility or define a TypedDict for the expected metadata structure

title: Import organization inconsistency
description: The codebase mixes absolute imports (from pydantic import BaseModel) and would benefit from relative imports for intra-package imports. models/findings.py imports from models.evolution which works but could use relative imports for better refactoring support.
suggested_fix: Use relative imports within the models package: from .evolution import EvolutionReport. This makes the package more refactoring-friendly and explicit about intra-package dependencies.

title: Duplicated utc_now() function across model files
description: The utc_now() function is defined identically in three separate files: models/builds.py, models/program.py, and models/runtime.py. This violates the DRY principle and creates maintenance burden - any change to datetime handling must be made in three places.
suggested_fix: Create a shared utility module (e.g., models/_utils.py) with a single utc_now() implementation and import it where needed.

title: Models used as both DTOs and domain objects
description: According to cross-segment findings, the route modules directly use these Pydantic models (AuditRequest, BuildRun, etc.) as DTOs for API requests/responses. There's no separation between API-facing DTOs and internal domain models. The findings.py imports EvolutionReport from models.evolution, showing models depend on other models, creating implicit domain coupling.
suggested_fix: Consider introducing a layer separation: create explicit DTO schemas in a separate package (e.g., schemas/api/) while keeping domain models in models/. Alternatively, add clear documentation that these models serve dual purposes.

title: No centralized enum definitions
description: Enums are scattered across multiple model files: LogLevel, AgentName, SSEEventType in agent_log.py; BuildStatus, TaskStatus, GateType in builds.py; Severity, Category, FindingSource in findings.py, etc. This makes it difficult to discover and reuse enumerations, and creates potential inconsistency in enum naming conventions and usage.
suggested_fix: Consider creating a centralized enums module (models/enums.py or models/_enums/) that exports all enumerations, or group related enums with their respective domain areas.

title: Missing module-level exports via __init__.py
description: The models directory lacks an __init__.py file to provide clear public API surface. External code must import specific modules (from models.builds import BuildRun) rather than using package-level exports. This exposes internal file structure and makes refactoring more difficult.
suggested_fix: Add models/__init__.py with explicit exports: __all__ = ['BuildRun', 'BuildStatus', 'DagNode', ...] to define stable public API.

title: Large BuildRun model with too many responsibilities
description: The BuildRun model in builds.py aggregates 11 different collections (task_runs, replan_history, debt_items, policy_violations, state_transitions, gate_history, etc.) making it a God object. This model serves as both configuration, state container, and event history, violating single responsibility principle.

title: Mutable default arguments in Pydantic models

Some fields use default_factory while others rely on Pydantic's automatic handling. Additionally, the utc_now default factory captures module-level function which could behave unexpectedly if modules are reloaded in different contexts.

title: OAuth State Secret Falls Back to JWT Secret
description: In config.py, the github_oauth_state_secret field has a default value of None. When this is None, the OAuth flow in api/routes/github_oauth.py falls back to using settings.supabase_jwt_secret for signing OAuth state tokens. Reusing the JWT secret for OAuth state creates a cryptographic confusion risk - if the JWT secret is compromised, both JWT authentication and OAuth state signing are compromised. Additionally, using the same secret for different purposes violates the principle of secret separation.

suggested_fix: Make github_oauth_state_secret a required field (remove None default) or add validation to fail startup if it's not set. Generate a cryptographically random secret specific to OAuth state signing.

title: Webhook Secret Has No Required Validation
description: The github_webhook_secret in config.py can be None. Webhook endpoints typically require a secret for signature verification to prevent spoofed webhook events. If this is None, the webhook verification logic (in api/routes/webhook.py based on neighbor findings) likely skips signature verification entirely, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary webhook events.
suggested_fix: Make github_webhook_secret a required field (remove None default) and enforce signature verification in the webhook handler.

title: Insufficient Rate Limit for API Endpoints
description: The rate_limit_per_minute is set to 10 across all endpoints. This generic limit may be too restrictive for legitimate bulk operations while still being insufficient for brute-force protection on authentication endpoints. Additionally, the rate limiting implementation uses get_remote_address which is vulnerable to IP spoofing (as noted in neighbor findings), allowing attackers to bypass limits.
suggested_fix: Implement tiered rate limiting: more restrictive for auth endpoints (login, OAuth), less restrictive for data operations. Configure trusted proxy headers properly to prevent IP spoofing.

title: CORS Allows HTTP Origins in Production
description: The CORS configuration allows both HTTP and HTTPS origins matching localhost or 127.0.0.1. While this is restricted to localhost, using HTTP (without TLS) in any context could allow credential theft via network interception. Additionally, the regex pattern allows any port on localhost/127.0.0.1 which could be exploited if there's a local proxy or DNS rebinding attack.
suggested_fix: Restrict CORS to HTTPS origins only in production environments. Consider implementing explicit allowed origins list rather than regex patterns.

title: Weak Default for FORGE AgentField API Key
description: The agentfield_api_key has an empty string default (""), which is different from None. This means the configuration will accept an empty string as a valid key, potentially causing silent authentication failures when FORGE integration is enabled. An empty string key would fail against the external service but might not be caught until runtime.
suggested_fix: Either make this a required field with Field(...) or validate that if forge_enabled is True, agentfield_api_key must be non-empty.

title: Debug Mode Potentially Exposed via Environment
description: While debug defaults to False in config.py, it can be overridden via environment variables. If debug=True is set in production, it could expose detailed error traces, StackOverflowException details, and application internals through the error responses.
suggested_fix: Add validation to ensure debug=False in production environments, or add a startup check that warns/fails if debug=True is set with non-localhost hosts.

title: OAuth State Secret Can Be None Leading to Runtime Errors
description: In config.py, the `github_oauth_state_secret` and `github_webhook_secret` fields are defined as `str | None = None`. When these are None and the code attempts to use them for cryptographic operations (e.g., HMAC signing in github_oauth.py), it will fail at runtime with a TypeError. The Settings class should enforce that these secrets are provided in production environments or raise validation errors at startup rather than failing at runtime.
suggested_fix: Use Pydantic field validation with a validator that ensures required secrets are provided when the corresponding feature is enabled. For example: `Field(None, validation_alias=...)` with a validator that raises if the feature is enabled but the secret is missing.

title: Missing Numeric Range Validation on Resource Limits
description: Configuration fields like `sandbox_cpu`, `sandbox_memory_gb`, `sandbox_disk_gb`, `sandbox_timeout_minutes`, `llm_max_output_tokens`, and rate limits accept any integer value including negative numbers. There's no validation that ensures these values are positive. This could lead to runtime errors or unexpected behavior if misconfigured.

title: Global Exception Handler Hides Error Details in Production
description: The global_exception_handler in main.py catches all exceptions and returns a generic 'Internal server error' message. The handler logs the exception but the logged information may not be accessible in all deployment environments.

Also, consider adding specific exception handlers for common exceptions (ValueError, ValidationError, etc.) to provide more meaningful error responses.

title: Permissive CORS Configuration for Development
description: The CORS middleware allows credentials from any localhost or 127.0.0.1 URL on any port. This is overly permissive for a production application. While appropriate for development, there's no conditional logic to tighten this in production environments based on the debug flag or an explicit allowed origins list.
suggested_fix: Add conditional CORS configuration based on settings.debug or an explicit allowed_origins list. For production, use an explicit list of allowed domains rather than a catch-all regex. Consider adding environment-specific configuration for allowed origins.

This would allow the application to start even if settings validation fails, providing better error messages. Alternatively, document this behavior clearly and ensure CI/CD validates settings at startup.

title: Inconsistent Field Definition Style for Required vs Optional
description: The Settings class mixes two styles for defining required fields: some use `Field(...)` (e.g., supabase_url) while others use type annotation with default values. Optional fields use `str | None = None` which is not consistent with the older `Optional[str] = None` style used in some route code.

title: Health Endpoint Lacks Authentication Bypass Verification

title: Global Singleton Settings Object Creates Tight Coupling
description: The config.py module creates a global singleton `settings = Settings()` at module level. suggested_fix: Use dependency injection with a settings factory pattern. Create a get_settings() function that returns Settings instances, allowing for configuration overrides in tests. Consider using a lazy initialization pattern or a settings manager class that can be mocked.

async def parse_repo_url(url: str) -> tuple[str, str]:

title: Missing Rate Limiting on ContextStore Operations
description: The ContextStore class provides unbounded storage for session data without any rate limiting or size restrictions on keys or values. Combined with findings from neighboring segments showing unbounded memory growth in SSE event buses, this could contribute to memory exhaustion attacks.
suggested_fix: Add size limits to the ContextStore: 1) Limit total number of keys stored, 2) Limit individual value sizes, 3) Implement TTL-based expiration for entries, 4) Add validation to ensure keys follow the documented namespace convention (e.g., 'file:', 'findings:', etc.).

title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Supabase Client Functions
description: The supabase_client.py contains multiple functions that handle sensitive data (github_access_token, project_charter, etc.) and pass them directly to the database without apparent encryption. The save_github_connection function stores tokens in plain text. Cross-reference: The OAuth state secret fallback issue from neighboring segments suggests a pattern of mishandling secrets.

title: Race Condition in Quota Check Not Present But Related Pattern Exists
description: The neighboring segment findings indicate a race condition in quota checks in api/routes/audit.py. While this segment (services) doesn't directly contain the race condition, the supabase_client.py provides increment_free_reports_generated which could be used in a non-atomic manner. The pattern of check-then-act is present in the dependent code.

locations.snippet:
async def increment_free_reports_generated(user_id: str, month_key: date) -> int:
    """Increment free-tier reports_generated counter and return new value."""
    row = await get_or_create_free_usage_month(user_id, month_key)
    current = int(row.get("reports_generated") or 0)
    next_value = current + 1

    client = _client()
    client.table("free_usage_monthly").update(
        {"reports_generated": next_value}
    ).eq("id", row["id"]).execute()
    return next_value

suggested_fix: This function reads the current value, increments in Python, then writes back - this is a read-modify-write that can race. Use an atomic SQL increment instead: client.table('free_usage_monthly').update({'reports_generated': supabase.sql('reports_generated + 1')}).eq('id', row['id']).execute() or use a database function with atomic increment.

title: Missing Authentication Check in Context Store
description: The ContextStore class stores and retrieves data based on scan_id (UUID) without any authentication or authorization checks. Any code with access to a scan_id can read or modify any stored data. This is related to the finding from neighboring segments about missing authorization on SSE status endpoints.
suggested_fix: The ContextStore should be scoped to a specific user context. Add user_id validation to ensure that data can only be accessed by the user who owns the scan. Consider integrating user context into the store's access patterns or adding an authorization layer before store operations.

title: Test Coverage Gap: Race Condition in Quota Checks Not Verified
description: The tests verify quota enforcement behavior but do not test for race conditions in concurrent quota operations. The neighbor segment findings indicate that quota checks in api/routes/audit.py are not atomic - the check and increment operations can have a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) gap. While tests verify the happy path and error paths for quota limits, concurrent request scenarios that could exploit this race condition are not covered.
suggested_fix: Add concurrent integration tests that simulate multiple simultaneous audit requests approaching the quota limit to verify atomicity of quota checks and increments. Use threading or async concurrent requests to verify that quota enforcement cannot be bypassed through race conditions.

title: Test Coverage Gap: Authorization on Action Item Access Not Verified
description: The tests for the fix route verify various error conditions (not found, in progress, project not found) but do not verify that a user cannot access action items belonging to other users. The neighbor findings indicate that api/routes/fix.py:trigger_fix retrieves an action_item without verifying ownership. Tests should verify that users can only access their own action items.
suggested_fix: Add test cases that verify: 1) User A cannot trigger a fix on User B's action_item_id, 2) The endpoint validates that the authenticated user owns the action_item before processing. Mock db.get_action_item to return an action_item with a different user_id and verify 403 Forbidden is returned.

title: Test Coverage Gap: SSE Status Endpoint Missing Ownership Verification
description: While the tests cover audit routes and artifact retrieval, there are no tests for the SSE status endpoint (/api/status/{scan_id}) which neighbor findings indicate lacks user ownership verification. Any authenticated user could potentially stream status for any scan_id.
suggested_fix: Add test cases for SSE status endpoint that verify: 1) User can only stream status for their own scans, 2) Accessing another user's scan_id returns 403/404. This would require testing the stream_status endpoint from api/routes/status.py.

title: Test Coverage Gap: Webhook Replay Detection Scaling Not Verified
description: The tests verify webhook replay detection works within a single test instance (using setUp to clear _seen_deliveries), but do not verify that replay detection works across multiple API instances. The neighbor findings indicate _seen_deliveries uses in-memory storage which doesn't scale horizontally.
suggested_fix: Add a note or integration test documenting that webhook replay detection currently only works within a single API instance. For production deployments requiring multiple instances, consider using a distributed cache (Redis) for _seen_deliveries.

title: Test Coverage Gap: OAuth State Secret Reuse Not Tested
description: The tests for GitHub OAuth verify the happy path but do not test the fallback behavior where OAuth state secret falls back to JWT secret. Neighbor findings indicate that _state_secret() falls back to supabase_jwt_secret which is a security concern.
suggested_fix: Add test case that mocks settings.github_oauth_state_secret as None/unset and verifies the system either: 1) Uses a separate secure default, or 2) Refuses to operate without explicit configuration (fail closed).

title: Potential Information Disclosure in FORGE Integration Tests
description: The test_forge_bridge.py tests send tier1_findings including severity levels to external FORGE service. While this is test code, it demonstrates that findings with severity 'critical' are sent to an external service. If production code follows this pattern, sensitive finding details could be exposed to external services.
suggested_fix: Verify that production code sanitizes or filters sensitive data before sending to external FORGE service. Consider whether severity levels and finding titles should be sent externally, or if only anonymized/faggregated data should be transmitted.

title: Test environment setup causes side effects at import time
description: Multiple test files set environment variables using os.environ.setdefault() at module import time (lines 11-17 in test_audit_routes.py, similar pattern in other test files). This causes side effects during import that can leak between test modules and affect other tests running in the same Python process. Additionally, the fake orchestrator module creation (lines 25-35) modifies sys.modules during import, which is a global side effect.
suggested_fix: Move environment variable setup to a pytest fixture with autouse=True or to a conftest.py file. Create the fake orchestrator in a test fixture that uses monkeypatch to temporarily modify sys.modules and cleans up afterward. Use pytest-env or similar plugin for environment variable management.

title: Tests directly access production module global state
description: Test files directly access internal module state such as audit.settings, fix.settings, webhook._seen_deliveries. In test_webhook_routes.py line 94, the test calls webhook._seen_deliveries.clear() in setUp, directly manipulating production module internals. This creates tight coupling between tests and implementation details - any refactoring of internal state will break tests.
suggested_fix: Instead of accessing internal state, inject a cleanup mechanism into the production code (e.g., a function like reset_replay_detection() or use dependency injection). Alternatively, expose configuration for test isolation through a proper interface.

title: Duplicated FastAPI test app setup across test classes
description: Each test file (test_audit_routes.py, test_fix_routes.py, test_github_oauth_routes.py, test_onboarding_routes.py, test_webhook_routes.py) contains nearly identical FastAPI app setup code in setUpClass: creating app, setting up limiter, adding middleware to inject user_id, including router. This violates DRY and creates maintenance burden - any change to test app setup must be replicated across 5+ files.
suggested_fix: Create a shared test fixture in conftest.py that returns a TestClient with properly configured app. Use pytest fixtures with proper scoping to avoid test pollution. Example: @pytest.fixture(scope="class") def audit_client(): ... that can be parameterized for different routers.

title: Test uses hardcoded mock paths brittle to refactoring
description: Tests use hardcoded module paths for mocking like 'api.routes.audit.db.get_github_access_token', 'api.routes.fix.db.get_action_item', etc. These string-based patches are tightly coupled to the specific import paths in production code. If the production code refactors imports (e.g., moves db to a different module or uses dependency injection), all these mock paths will break.
suggested_fix: Consider using dependency injection in production code to allow injecting mock implementations. Alternatively, create a test db interface that can be patched at a higher level. Use unittest.mock.patch.object when possible instead of string-based paths.

title: Fake orchestrator workaround indicates production dependency issue
description: In test_audit_routes.py lines 25-35, a fake orchestrator module is created and inserted into sys.modules to prevent importing the deep orchestrator that requires 'openhands'. This is a workaround for a production code problem: the api.routes.audit module has an unwanted dependency on the orchestrator that shouldn't exist in Tier 1 context. This creates hidden test complexity and indicates layering violation in production code.
suggested_fix: Refactor production code to remove direct import of orchestrator in audit routes - use lazy imports or dependency injection. The audit route should only import tier1-specific modules, not the deep orchestrator. Consider creating an abstraction layer so the route doesn't know which orchestrator is being used.

title: Test directly couples to implementation details like limiter
description: Tests access internal implementation details like audit.limiter, fix.limiter and assign them to app.state. This couples tests tightly to FastAPI implementation and internal module structure. If limiter is moved, refactored, or replaced, tests will break.
suggested_fix: Create a fixture that handles limiter setup transparently, or make the limiter optional/fallback in production code so tests can omit it. Consider checking if limiter exists before assignment: if hasattr(audit, 'limiter'): app.state.limiter = audit.limiter
